status_summary: No proposed or final rule amending the child labor hazardous occupations orders was found since 2025-01-20. The Federal Register search of Labor Department documents for child labor returned only a joint employer proposal (2026-04-23) and a proposal on removing non-notice-and-comment interpretive provisions (2025-07-02). A trade-press report of the Wage and Hour Division head's March 2026 remarks described a priority on enforcement against the worst forms of child labor, including minors in dangerous jobs. Two narrow logging bills introduced on 2025-02-11, H.R. 1193 and S. 509, concern 16 and 17 year olds in timber harvesting by statute and have had no action beyond committee referral.

timeline.event: H.R. 1193 (Future in Logging Careers Act) and S. 509 (Future Logging Careers Act) were introduced and referred to the House Education and Workforce and Senate HELP Committees; they address FLSA child labor coverage of 16 and 17 year olds in timber harvesting, with an exception for parent-owned operations. No further action is recorded; this is related legislation, not a DOL hazard-order amendment.

title: Amend child labor hazard orders so teens can do regulated jobs with training and consent
uncertainties: No proposed or final rule amending the child labor hazardous occupations orders was found.
